Each body of texts, or corpus, is used to fit two complimentary topic models. Results from this process are used to determine the importance of pre-determined categories within each corpus. These categories, shown in Figure 32, are considered to be analogous to the perceptions of fleet managers during the MDHD purchasing decision. Discussion and conclusions focus on identifying insights into the differences between topic saliency and perceptions from these two bodies of texts, but also demonstrates the use of these types of topic models as inputs into agent- based models (ABM) of MDHD EV adoption. Theory and Application of Machine Learning Tools Recent work demonstrates how insights gathered from interviews can be consolidated to rank perceptions.97 The present investigation improves upon these baseline ranking methods by increasing the robustness of the preprocessing steps of latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) and incorporating a deep learning approach, BERTopic98, that can be combined with the LDA results. LDA Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) is an unsupervised topic modeling algorithm. The present application of LDA is based on the algorithm as presented in Ouren et al., 2023. To summarize this previous presentation, the input to LDA is a set of documents (a corpus), and the output from LDA is a topic model. This work uses LDA as an integral part of the process because LDA can rank multiple relevant topics in a document using the metric of saliency. BERTopic Bi-directional Encoder Representations of Transformers-Topic (BERTopic) is a topic modeling approach that is based on the foundational BERT model, but adds two more steps to create a topic model output similar to that of LDA. It is used here due to its successful implementation relative to topic modeling benchmark problems99. The main job of BERT in BERTopic is to create embeddings from sentences. These embeddings are numerical vectors that capture the meaning of the sentence.
